Voting Information

  1. Vote at Home (Absentee)

Vote in the convenience of your home to save time, skip the lines or bad weather. Voters who are currently registered in Natrona County may request an absentee ballot beginning
January 1 of each election year. Absentee ballots can not be requested on the day of the election. To request a ballot, fill out our online Absentee Ballot Request Form, call the Elections Office at 307-235-9217 or visit the office at:

200 N. Center St. 
Room 154
Casper, WY 82601

Ballots will be mailed from the County Clerk's Office 28 days in advance of the specified election. The completed ballot must be returned to the County Clerk's Office by 7:00 pm on Election Day. Ballots may NOT be returned to a polling place. You must request an absentee ballot each election year.

Tips for voting absentee

  • Vote the ballot with an ordinary black ink pen. Do not use a marker or gel pen as they bleed through the ballot paper.
  • Please be sure to sign and date the back of the ballot envelope confirming you are the voter of this ballot. If this envelope is not signed, the ballot will be rejected and not tabulated.
  • Ballots may be delivered in person to our office or returned by mail. Please allow 7 - 10 days for your ballot to arrive and 7-10 days for it to be returned to us if mailing the ballot.

Want to know when your mail ballot will arrive? Preview your mail before it arrives by signing up for USPS "informed delivery". For more on the free service, visit the USPS Informed Delivery website.

  1. Vote Early In Person

Vote Early - Bring your voter ID

Voting early is a popular option for many voters. Early voting starts 28 days before the election and ends the day before the election. Early voting takes place at the Natrona County Clerk's Office:

200 N. Center St.
Room 154
Casper, WY 82601

Early voting for the 2026 General Election begins October 6th and ends November 2nd. The Elections Office will be open for early voting from 8:00 am - 5:00 pm, Monday thru Friday. You can also register to vote when you come to the Elections Office for early voting. Please make sure you bring all required documentation with you.

  1. Vote on Election Day

You can vote at your designated Polling Location on Election Day from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm. Please bring your ID with you (see list below). You can also register to vote at your Polling Location on Election Day with the required documents.

To find out where your Polling Location is and view Sample ballots, use our Where Do I Vote tool. 

  1. Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA)

Absentee ballots for those qualifying under UOCAVA are sent 45 days prior to an election. Ballots must be returned by mail and received in the Clerk's Office no later than 7:00 pm on Election Day in order to be counted. Voted ballots cannot be returned by email.

You can also send your FPCA by email to the Elections Department.

Visit the Federal Voting Assistance Program website for more information regarding eligibility, voting residence and more.

Voter ID

Wyoming law requires voters to present an acceptable form of identification when voting early or on Election Day. Acceptable forms of identification include:

  • Wyoming driver's license or ID card
  • Tribal ID card
  • Valid U.S. passport
  • U.S. military card
  • Driver's license or ID card from another state
  • University of Wyoming student ID
  • Wyoming community college student ID
  • Wyoming public school student ID
  • Valid Medicare insurance card*
  • Valid Medicaid insurance card*
  • Valid Wyoming concealed firearm permit

* Medicare and Medicaid insurance cards will no longer be an acceptable form of identification for voting purposes after December 31, 2029.

If you do not have one of the documents listed above, you may obtain a free Wyoming ID card from Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services (PDF).
